title: Common
description: Shapes used by more than one entity.

type.description: The scheme, such as CNPJ, CPF, NIF, VAT or EIN. Free text, always stated, never inferred from the length of the value.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, when the scheme does not imply one.

contactPoint.title: ContactPoint
contactPoint.description: One way to reach an actor.

type.description: Which channel the value is for.

value.description: An address, or a number in E.164 digits including the country code.

locale.description: The language to write to this point in.

localIds.title: LocalIds
localIds.description: The id this actor has in each system that holds a record of it, keyed by system name. Used while it has no wallet.

embedding.description: A semantic vector of whatever it hangs on. Derived, and meaningful only to the model and the dimension that produced it, so it may well not travel: a reader holding another model recomputes it from the text rather than trusting this one. No length is fixed here, because the length is the embedding model's and changes with it.

metadata.description: Whatever the producer recorded about the thing, as it read it. The keys belong to whoever wrote them — a format, an extractor, a splitter — so none are fixed here and no reader should expect a particular one.

assetType.title: AssetType
assetType.description: What kind of thing an asset is, which decides which pipeline reads it. A document covers an article, a PDF, or raw text.

processingStatus.title: ProcessingStatus
processingStatus.description: Where a pipeline stands on the thing it was given. Which move from which is a rule held beside the type, never in it.

storedFile.title: StoredFile
storedFile.description: Bytes somebody is keeping, pointed at rather than carried. Never the file itself: the store that holds it holds it, and this says which key to ask under and, while it lasts, where it can be fetched. Nothing is required, because a file can be known by its key before any address has been issued for it, and served by an address before anybody recorded a key.

storageKey.description: Where the bytes sit in the store that holds them. The lasting handle, meaningful only to that store: a reader asks the store, never resolves the key itself.

url.description: Where the file can be fetched right now. Often signed and short-lived, so it is read at the moment of use and never kept as the address of the file.

sizeBytes.description: How big it is, so whoever is about to fetch it knows what they are asking for.

ragSource.title: RagSource
ragSource.description: One retrieved chunk an answer leaned on, as it was at the time of the answer. A pointer plus what a person needs to judge it — never the chunk, which stays with the asset it came from — so the citation still reads once the chunk has changed.

asset.description: The asset the chunk came from, as the system that owns the asset names it.

chunk.description: The chunk itself, as the system that owns the chunk names it.

score.description: How close the chunk sat to the question, as the retrieval scored it. Comparable inside one search, not across searches: the scale belongs to the model that searched.

chunkType.description: Which part of the asset the chunk is — a summary, a transcript, a block of article text. Free text: the vocabulary belongs to whoever chunks.

excerpt.description: The opening of the chunk, carried so a person can see what was cited without fetching it.

assetTitle.description: What the parent asset was called when the answer was written. Kept as a copy on purpose: a citation should still read after the asset is retitled.

thumbnailUrl.description: A picture of the parent asset, when the system that serves it offers one. Derived, and resolvable only against the deploy that built it.

creativeReading.title: CreativeReading
creativeReading.description: What a model made of a piece of work: how it sat against the voice it was written for, how it fitted the channel it was written into, and why. About the work, never about whoever asked for it — nothing here is said about an actor, so none of it is testimony.

brandVoiceScore.description: How close the work came to the voice it was written for, from 0 to 1. The range is what the scorer produces, and keeping a number inside it is the job of the code that writes the record.

channelFitScore.description: How well the work fitted the channel it was written into, from 0 to 1, on the same scale.

overallScore.description: The single number carried alongside the two others, from 0 to 1. Stated rather than derived here: how the scorer weighed voice against fit is its own, and recomputing it elsewhere would invent a weighting nobody agreed to.

reasoning.description: Why those numbers, in the scorer's own words. Kept because a number with no account of itself cannot be argued with.
